questions.question: Dr. Budhri Tati, named for the Padma Shri in the Padma Awards announced in 2026, is linked to which of the following areas of contribution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social Work**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Budhri Tati**, a prominent figure from the **Bastar** region in **Chhattisgarh**, was announced as a recipient of the **Padma Shri** award in **2026** for her lifelong dedication to the marginalized sections of society.
 
• She has been a pioneer in providing **healthcare** and **nutritional support** to the tribal population, particularly the **Mariya** and **Muria** tribes, for more than **four decades**.
 
• Her work is primarily categorized under **Social Work** because she operates in remote, **Naxal-affected** areas where institutional medical reach is limited, often providing services **free of cost** or at a very nominal rate.
 
• She has played a significant role in reducing **maternal mortality** and **infant mortality** rates in her district by blending traditional knowledge with modern medical practices.
 
• Her recognition highlights the **Government of India’s** focus on honoring "Unsung Heroes" who work at the **grassroots level** for the upliftment of the **underprivileged**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Padma Awards:** Established in the **year 1954**, these are among the highest **civilian honors** of **India**. They are announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (**26th January**) and conferred by the **President of India** at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**.
 
• **Categories of Awards:** The awards are given in three categories: **Padma Vibhushan** (for exceptional and distinguished service), **Padma Bhushan** (for distinguished service of high order), and **Padma Shri** (for distinguished service in any field).
 
• **Social Work Category:** This field includes contributions to **orphanages**, **charitable institutions**, **community service**, **healthcare for the poor**, and **environment protection**. Dr. Tati's medical service is classified here due to its **philanthropic** nature.
 
• **Literature and Education:** This category honors **authors**, **journalists**, **poets**, and **educators** for their excellence in writing and teaching. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **Science and Engineering:** This field recognizes **scientists** and **engineers** for **technological innovations**, **space research**, and **nuclear energy** developments. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Trade and Industry:** This category is reserved for **entrepreneurs**, **industrialists**, and **business leaders** who contribute to the **economy** and **employment generation** in **India**. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Impact:** Dr. Budhri Tati's efforts in **Chhattisgarh** have not only improved **public health** but also fostered a sense of trust between the **tribal communities** and **social welfare** initiatives. *Hence, statement C is correct.*
 
• **Selection Process:** The **Padma Awards Committee**, headed by the **Cabinet Secretary** and including the **Home Secretary**, makes recommendations to the **Prime Minister** and the **President** for the final selection.
 
• **Facts and Figures:** In **2026**, the list of awardees emphasized **diversity** and **inclusion**, featuring a significant number of **women** and **tribal activists** from across the **country**.
 
• **Application of Services:** The **functions** performed by Dr. Tati include **maternal care**, **herbal medicine research**, and **village sanitation** drives, which are classic **applications** of holistic **Social Work**.

questions.question: What is the name of the first-ever results-based environmental award launched by India in 2026 to incentivize verifiable pollution reduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero Prize.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Government of India has officially launched the 'Zero Prize' to encourage measurable environmental protection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Zero Prize is India's first results-based environmental award, meaning it only recognizes actual, verified reductions in pollution.**
 
• It is designed to move away from rewarding "efforts" and instead reward **measurable outcomes** in air, water, and land quality.
 
• The prize pool is **₹5 crore**, with specific allocations for successful interventions in three primary categories.
 
• The initiative aligns with India's **net-zero 2070** goal and the Swachh Bharat Mission.
 
• Zero Prize Framework__
 __
 
• Goal - Reach "Zero" pollution levels through innovation.
 
• Method - Third-party scientific monitoring and audits.
 
• Scope - Air, Water, and Land/Soil.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Results-Based Award__

 __
 
• A system where the incentive is provided only after the **result is achieved and verified** by an independent agency.
 
 
 
• Mission LiFE__
 __
 
• A global movement led by India to encourage sustainable lifestyles and environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• Pollution Monitoring__
 __
 
• Uses tools like the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** and water quality parameters (BOD/COD) to measure the success of applicants.
 
 
 
• Incentivization__
 
 
• Encouraging startups and companies to invest in **green technology** by providing high-value financial rewards.

questions.question: Which noted literary personality has been conferred with the 58th Jnanpith award in the year 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagadguru Rambhadracharya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jagadguru Rambhadracharya**, a renowned Indian scholar, poet, and spiritual leader, was conferred the prestigious **58th Jnanpith Award** in 2025 for his exceptional contribution to Sanskrit literature.
 
• He has authored more than 120 books and texts in Sanskrit, Hindi, and other languages, including epic poetry, plays, and commentaries on ancient Indian scriptures.
 
• Jagadguru Rambhadracharya is a visually impaired polymath who has dedicated his life to promoting Indian culture, literature, and spirituality.
 
• His works include modern interpretations of the **Ramayana** and the **Bhagavad Gita**, along with other significant contributions to Vedic literature and philosophy.
 
• The **Jnanpith Award** is India's highest literary honor, presented annually by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization to an author for their outstanding contribution to literature in any of the 22 scheduled languages of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhash Mukhopadhyay**:

 
 
• Subhash Mukhopadhyay was a prominent Bengali poet and writer, known for his contributions to modern Bengali poetry.
 
• He was honored with the Jnanpith Award in 1991 for his significant contributions to Indian literature.
 
• His works often focused on social issues, human emotions, and the struggles of the common man.
 
 
 
• **Vinod Kumar Shukla**:
 
 
• Vinod Kumar Shukla is a renowned Hindi writer known for his unique style of storytelling and poetic prose.
 
• He received the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Jnanpith Award in 2019 for his novel "*Deewar Mein Ek Khidki Rehti Thi*."
 
• His works often explore the themes of rural life, human relationships, and existential dilemmas.
 
 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh**:
 
 
• Amitav Ghosh is one of India's most celebrated contemporary authors, known for his contributions to English literature.
 
• He was honored with the 54th Jnanpith Award in 2018, becoming the first English-language writer to receive this distinction.
 
• His notable works include "*The Shadow Lines*," "*The Glass Palace*," and "*The Ibis Trilogy*."
 
• Ghosh's writing often delves into themes of colonialism, migration, environmental challenges, and cultural intersections.
 
 
 
• **Jnanpith Award**:
 
 
• The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honor, instituted in 1961 by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization.
 
• It is awarded annually to an author for their outstanding contribution to literature in any of the 22 scheduled languages listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• The recipient is selected by a committee of literary experts and receives a cash prize, a citation plaque, and a bronze replica of Goddess Saraswati.

questions.question: Which mission was honored with the prestigous 2026 Goddard Astronautics Award by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandrayaan-3**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• India’s **Chandrayaan-3** lunar mission has been honoured with the prestigious **2026 Goddard Astronautics Award** by the **American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The award was presented in **Washington DC** on **May 21**, during the **AIAA ASCEND 2026 Conference**.
 
• **Chandrayaan-3** was recognized for its historic achievement on **August 23, 2023**, when it became the first spacecraft to achieve a **soft landing** near the **Moon’s south pole**.
 
• The mission delivered critical data and confirmed the presence of key chemical elements in the lunar south polar soil, supporting future human missions.
 
• India’s Ambassador to the United States, **Vinay Kwatra**, accepted the award on behalf of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• Other options like **Mangalyaan-2**, **Aditya-L1**, and **Gaganyaan-1** are distinct ISRO missions but were not the recipients of this specific 2026 award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Goddard Astronautics Award** is the highest honour **AIAA** bestows for notable achievements in the field of **astronautics**.
 
• It was endowed by Mrs. Goddard to commemorate **Robert H. Goddard**, a rocket visionary and pioneer.
 
• The award took its current form in **1975**, broadening its selection criteria beyond engineering science.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The acceptance speech highlighted **Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Space Vision 2047**, emphasizing India's roadmap for deep space exploration.
 
• The recognition underscores the deepening partnership between **India and the United States** in space exploration.

• Other nominees like **Leon Thomas**, **Addison Rae**, and **Lola Young** were also strong contenders who demonstrated exceptional growth in their respective genres, but **Olivia Dean**'s overall impact and artistic breakthrough were deemed the most significant by the **Recording Academy** voters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Recording Academy:**

 
 
• Founded in **1957**, it is a **United States**-based organization of music professionals, including performers, songwriters, producers, and engineers. It is the body responsible for organizing the **Grammy Awards**.
 
• The **Recording Academy** aims to improve the cultural condition and quality of life for music and its makers. Its headquarters are located in **Santa Monica**, **California**.
 
 
 
• **Grammy Award History:**
 
 
• The first **Grammy Awards** ceremony was held on **May 4, 1959**, simultaneously in **Los Angeles** and **New York City**. It was originally called the **Gramophone Awards**.
 
• The trophy is a **gilded gramophone**, handcrafted by **Billings Artworks** in **Colorado**. It represents excellence in the recording arts and sciences.
 
 
 
• **Nomination and Voting Process:**
 
 
• Entries are submitted by members and record companies. They are then screened for **eligibility** and **genre placement** by experts.
 
• The voting is conducted by **Voting Members** of the **Recording Academy**, ensuring a **peer-reviewed** selection process that emphasizes technical proficiency and artistic integrity over chart positions or sales figures.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• **Los Angeles** serves as the primary hub for the ceremony, reflecting its status as a global center for the entertainment and music industry. The **68th Grammys** continued this tradition, drawing thousands of international industry leaders to the city.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Best New Artist Evolution:** Over the years, the **Recording Academy** has updated the rules for this category to reflect the changing nature of the music industry, such as removing the strict limit on the number of albums released to accommodate the rise of **streaming** and **EPs**.
 
• **Cultural Impact:** Winning a **Grammy** often results in a significant "Grammy Bump," where an artist's **sales**, **streaming numbers**, and **touring opportunities** increase substantially due to the global visibility of the event.

questions.question: Recently who has been awarded ‘Woman of the Year’ by World Athletics?

__
 
• The legendary Indian long jumper **Anju Bobby George** was bestowed with the **Woman of the Year** award by **World Athletics** in **December 2021**.
 
• She was honored with this prestigious title for her constant voice against **gender inequality** and her efforts in advancing the sport of athletics in **India**.
 
• **Anju Bobby George** made history by becoming the first **Indian** athlete to win a medal at the **World Athletics Championships** when she secured the **bronze medal** in **long jump** in **2003** held in **Paris**.
 
• The award recognizes her immense contribution to the sport through her academy, the **Anju Bobby George Foundation**, which she opened in **2016** to train and mentor young girls, helping them reach the world stage in athletics.
 
• Beyond her competitive career, she serves as the **Senior Vice President** of the **Athletics Federation of India (AFI)**, where she continues to advocate for the rights and development of athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anju Bobby George:** Born on **19 April 1977** in **Changanassery, Kerala**, she is a world-renowned track and field athlete. Apart from her **2003** victory, she won the **Gold medal** at the **IAAF World Athletics Final** in **2005** in **Monte Carlo**. She represented India at the **2004 Athens Olympics**, finishing sixth with a personal best of **6.83m**.
 
• **Pusarla Venkata Sindhu (PV Sindhu):** She is a world-class **badminton** player from **Hyderabad, India**. She is the first **Indian** to become the **Badminton World Champion** and has won two consecutive **Olympic medals**—a **Silver** at the **2016 Rio Olympics** and a **Bronze** at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
• **Hima Das:** Popularly known as the **'Dhing Express'**, she is a sprinter from the state of **Assam**. She became the first **Indian** athlete to win a **Gold medal** in a track event at the **IAAF World U20 Championships** in **2018**, competing in the **400m** race.
 
• **Dutee Chand:** She is a professional sprinter from **Odisha** and is the national record holder in the women's **100m** sprint. She is a double **Silver medalist** at the **2018 Asian Games** and is the first **Indian** woman sprinter to win **Gold** at the **Universiade** (World University Games) in **2019**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

It was founded on **17 July 1912** and is currently headquartered in **Monaco**. The current President is **Sebastian Coe**.
 
• **National Recognition:** For her exemplary performance and contribution to sports, Anju Bobby George was awarded the **Arjuna Award** in **2002**, the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** (then Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) in **2003**, and the **Padma Shri** (India's fourth-highest civilian award) in **2004**.
